newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Coca-Cola CFO on Q3 provisions.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Coca-Cola CFO on Q3 provisions.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co Chief Financial Officer James Chestnut said on Tuesday that a newly announced reduction in concentrate inventory levels would lead to lower concentrate gallon sales in Europe, Africa and the Middle and Far East for the third quarter.

Reduced inventory levels among independent bottlers in those regions would bring about one of two $180-200 million quarterly provisions for the company and keep worldwide concentrate gallon sales flat for the three-month period.

"The Middle and Far East Group will be down between five and six percent. Europe is actually down the same percentage and Africa Group down 14-15 percent for the quarter," Chestnut told Reuters in an interview.

A second $180-200 million quarter provision would reflect a more aggressive marketing stance for Coca-Cola Foods' Minute Maid juice products and an accounting rationalisation of asset values for bottling operations and other segments of the concentrate business.
Between those after-tax provisions and three non-recurring items, Chestnut said Coke expected to earn $0.38-0.39 a share.
